claims.title: Bubi settle Bioko
claims.summary: Bantu-speaking peoples, ancestors of the Bubi, are held to have crossed from the mainland to the island later called Fernando Pó (Bioko) in successive waves, settling an island that earlier held Neolithic populations and developing a distinct island society.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1200-bubi-settle-bioko, claim TL:GNQ:event:1200:bubi-settle-bioko, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fang and Ndowe of Río Muni
claims.summary: The Fang, a large Bantu people, settled the forests of the mainland enclave of Río Muni, while Ndowe and related coastal peoples — later grouped as Playeros — occupied the shoreline and mediated trade with the interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1300-fang-and-ndowe-of-rio-muni, claim TL:GNQ:event:1300:fang-and-ndowe-of-rio-muni, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Annobón peopled from Angola
claims.summary: The remote island of Annobón, uninhabited before Atlantic navigation, was settled by Africans brought by the Portuguese largely from Angola via São Tomé; the Annobonese came to speak a Portuguese-based creole.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1450-annobon-peopled-from-angola, claim TL:GNQ:event:1450:annobon-peopled-from-angola, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fernão do Pó sights the island
claims.summary: The Portuguese navigator Fernão do Pó sighted the volcanic island in the Gulf of Guinea in 1472, reportedly naming it Formosa; it soon took his own name as Fernando Pó, the island later renamed Bioko.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1472-fernao-do-po-sights-the-island, claim TL:GNQ:event:1472:fernao-do-po-sights-the-island, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of El Pardo cedes the islands to Spain
claims.summary: By the Treaty of El Pardo, Portugal ceded Fernando Pó, Annobón and commercial rights on the adjacent African coast to Spain, in exchange for recognition of Portuguese claims in South America; Spain sought a base for the slave trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1778-treaty-of-el-pardo-cedes-the-islands-to-spain, claim TL:GNQ:event:1778:treaty-of-el-pardo-cedes-the-islands-to-spain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Argelejo expedition fails
claims.summary: A Spanish expedition under the Conde de Argelejo arrived to take possession but was broken by disease and disorder; Spain effectively abandoned the islands for decades, administering them on paper from its American viceroyalties.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1778-the-argelejo-expedition-fails, claim TL:GNQ:event:1778:the-argelejo-expedition-fails, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain founds an anti-slavery base at Port Clarence
claims.summary: With Spanish acquiescence, the Royal Navy under William Fitzwilliam Owen established a base on Fernando Pó in 1827, founding Port Clarence (later Santa Isabel/Malabo) to support the squadron suppressing the Atlantic slave trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1827-britain-founds-an-anti-slavery-base-at-port, claim TL:GNQ:event:1827:britain-founds-an-anti-slavery-base-at-port, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain withdraws to Sierra Leone
claims.summary: The British base on Fernando Pó was withdrawn to Sierra Leone in 1843, Spain having declined to sell its rights; freed Africans, Sierra Leoneans and other settlers remained as the English-speaking Fernandino community.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1843-britain-withdraws-to-sierra-leone, claim TL:GNQ:event:1843:britain-withdraws-to-sierra-leone, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spain installs effective rule under Carlos Chacón
claims.summary: Spain sent the naval officer Carlos Chacón as governor in 1858 to organise a colonial administration on Fernando Pó; Baptist missionaries established under the British were pressed to withdraw in favour of Spanish Catholic missions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1858-spain-installs-effective-rule-under-carlos, claim TL:GNQ:event:1858:spain-installs-effective-rule-under-carlos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Paris fixes Río Muni
claims.summary: The 1900 Treaty of Paris with France delimited Spain's mainland enclave of Río Muni at roughly 26,000 km², far smaller than Spain had claimed, setting the borders with French Cameroon and Gabon.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1900-treaty-of-paris-fixes-rio-muni, claim TL:GNQ:event:1900:treaty-of-paris-fixes-rio-muni, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Liberian labour treaty for the cocoa plantations
claims.summary: A 1914 treaty brought contract labourers from Liberia to Fernando Pó's cocoa plantations; an ILO inquiry in 1930 found the recruitment had occurred under "criminal compulsion" akin to slave raiding, and the Liberian supply was cut off.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1914-liberian-labour-treaty-for-the-cocoa-plantations, claim TL:GNQ:event:1914:liberian-labour-treaty-for-the-cocoa-plantations, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bioko and Río Muni united as Spanish Guinea
claims.summary: From 1926 Spain governed Fernando Pó and the mainland enclave of Río Muni together as the colony of Spanish Guinea, its economy resting on the cocoa plantations of the island.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1926-bioko-and-rio-muni-united-as-spanish-guinea, claim TL:GNQ:event:1926:bioko-and-rio-muni-united-as-spanish-guinea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Made an overseas "province" of Spain
claims.summary: In 1959 Spain reclassified the colony as the "Equatorial Region," divided into the provinces of Fernando Poo and Río Muni, with elected local representatives sent to the Spanish Cortes — a first step toward decolonisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1959-made-an-overseas-province-of-spain, claim TL:GNQ:event:1959:made-an-overseas-province-of-spain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Autonomy and the name Equatorial Guinea
claims.summary: A 1963 referendum approved a regime of autonomy granting limited internal self-government; the territory took the name Equatorial Guinea ahead of full independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1963-autonomy-and-the-name-equatorial-guinea, claim TL:GNQ:event:1963:autonomy-and-the-name-equatorial-guinea, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from Spain
claims.summary: After a 1968 constitutional referendum and September elections won by Francisco Macías Nguema, the Republic of Equatorial Guinea became independent from Spain on 12 October 1968, uniting Bioko, Río Muni and Annobón.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1968-independence-from-spain, claim TL:GNQ:event:1968:independence-from-spain, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Macías Nguema becomes first president
claims.summary: Francisco Macías Nguema, victor of the September 1968 elections, became Equatorial Guinea's first president at independence, soon concentrating power and beginning a slide into dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1968-macias-nguema-becomes-first-president, claim TL:GNQ:event:1968:macias-nguema-becomes-first-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: President for life
claims.summary: After establishing a single-party state in 1970 and gutting the constitution, Macías had himself declared president for life in 1972, ruling through a violent personality cult that dismantled churches, schools and much of the state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1972-president-for-life, claim TL:GNQ:event:1972:president-for-life, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mass killing and exile
claims.summary: Under Macías tens of thousands were killed — figures of roughly 35,000–50,000 deaths are commonly cited — and by 1979 around a quarter of the population had fled into exile; the Bubi and Nigerian workers were among those targeted. Figures remain estimates.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1972-mass-killing-and-exile, claim TL:GNQ:event:1972:mass-killing-and-exile, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cocoa economy collapses as labourers flee
claims.summary: Amid the terror, tens of thousands of Nigerian contract labourers were withdrawn from Fernando Pó's plantations in the mid-1970s, and cocoa production — the colony's economic mainstay — collapsed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1976-cocoa-economy-collapses-as-labourers-flee, claim TL:GNQ:event:1976:cocoa-economy-collapses-as-labourers-flee, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Obiang's coup overthrows Macías
claims.summary: On 3 August 1979 Macías's nephew, army officer Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, led a coup that overthrew the dictator after fighting that cost hundreds of lives.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1979-obiang-s-coup-overthrows-macias, claim TL:GNQ:event:1979:obiang-s-coup-overthrows-macias, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Macías executed
claims.summary: Captured and tried, Francisco Macías Nguema was executed by firing squad on 29 September 1979 along with several associates, ending eleven years of dictatorship; Obiang assumed the presidency.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1979-macias-executed, claim TL:GNQ:event:1979:macias-executed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Obiang takes power
claims.summary: Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo assumed the presidency after the 1979 coup and execution of Macías, and renamed the main islands Bioko and Annobón; he has remained in power ever since.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-1979-obiang-takes-power, claim TL:GNQ:event:1979:obiang-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zafiro oil field discovered
claims.summary: Mobil and partners discovered the major Zafiro oil field offshore Bioko Island in March 1995, the find that opened Equatorial Guinea's petroleum era.

sources.label: Zafiro Oil Field, Bioko Island, Gulf of Guinea

claims.title: Oil production begins
claims.summary: The Zafiro field came on-stream in August 1996, less than eighteen months after discovery, launching Equatorial Guinea as an oil producer; output later peaked in the hundreds of thousands of barrels a day.

sources.label: Zafiro Oil Field, Bioko Island, Gulf of Guinea

claims.title: The "Wonga Coup" foiled
claims.summary: An attempted coup by a group of foreign mercenaries — the so-called Wonga Coup, linked to Simon Mann — was foiled in 2004, underscoring the instability around oil-rich Equatorial Guinea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-2004-the-wonga-coup-foiled, claim TL:GNQ:event:2004:the-wonga-coup-foiled, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wealth amid deep inequality
claims.summary: Oil gave Equatorial Guinea one of Africa's highest GDP-per-capita figures, yet much of the population remained poor; the government faced sustained criticism over corruption, human rights and the concentration of wealth in the ruling family.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-2000-wealth-amid-deep-inequality, claim TL:GNQ:event:2000:wealth-amid-deep-inequality, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Joined, then delisted, by the transparency initiative
claims.summary: Equatorial Guinea joins the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative in February 2008 and is delisted in April 2010; a fresh application in October 2019 is refused by the EITI Board in February 2020.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-2008-joined-then-delisted-by-the-transparency, claim TL:GNQ:event:2008:joined-then-delisted-by-the-transparency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A capital in the rainforest
claims.summary: The government moves its headquarters from Malabo on Bioko to Ciudad de la Paz — Djibloho — an unfinished purpose-built city deep in the mainland forest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Equatorial Guinea: From the Bubi of Bioko and the Fang of Río Muni, through the Portuguese sighting of Fernando Pó, Spain's cocoa colony and a British anti-slavery base, to independence in 1968, the terror of Macías Nguema, the long rule of his nephew Obiang, and the oil wealth of the 1990s.", terralore.co/country/GNQ/chronicle#ev-2016-a-capital-in-the-rainforest, claim TL:GNQ:event:2016:a-capital-in-the-rainforest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
